discovery: Microscopic counting of black hole entropy from string theory and the resulting gauge/gravity (holographic) duality

nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

motivation: Bekenstein and Hawking showed that black holes carry entropy proportional to horizon area, but its microscopic origin remained a central puzzle of quantum gravity. In 1996 Strominger and Vafa counted the BPS bound states of D-branes and reproduced exactly the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, the first statistical derivation of black hole entropy from a quantum theory of gravity. Maldacena, working with Strominger, extended this to near-extremal black holes and Hawking emission, and in 1997 distilled these results into the AdS/CFT correspondence, an exact equivalence between gravity in anti-de Sitter space and a gauge theory on its boundary. Holography has since become a precise, quantitative tool: protected quantities such as superconformal indices now reproduce the entropy of AdS black holes, and the duality informs strongly coupled plasmas, condensed matter and quantum information. These works turned black hole thermodynamics into a sharp, testable statement about the quantum states of gravity.
